Population.evidence_source: Participants were eligible if they (1) had previous experiences of suicidality, (2) were at least 19 years old, (3) self-identifed as a gay, bisexual or two-spirit man, and (4) spoke English.

Type.evidence_source: The study used a photovoice methodology, an approach grounded in the traditions of community-based and participatory action research where individuals afected by an issue take and narrate photographs to describe their experiences and perspectives (Wang, 1999). This method was selected as suicide is highly stigmatized (Sudak, Maxim, & Carpenter, 2008), and photovoice can increase the feasibility of studying stigma ridden issues because it allows participants to discuss their experiences bypassing sole reliance on words (Olife & Bottorf, 2007; Wang, 1999). Following university ethics approval, participants were recruited through the distribution of posters within Vancouver's gay village and online via social media sites. The ads invited potential participants to contact the study team by email or telephone. Participants were eligible if they (1) had previous experiences of suicidality, (2) were at least 19 years old, (3) self-identifed as a gay, bisexual or two-spirit man, and (4) spoke English. Men who self-disclosed current suicidality were excluded from the study and referred to mental health services.

Area.evidence_source: Participants were asked to take photographs to illustrate their previous experiences of suicidality, including what they believed caused and/or triggered their suicide thoughts, the strategies they used to manage their suicidality, and their perspectives on GB2SM's suicide.
